content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp upward moves in history; apply a dampening factor (e.g., cap forecast at +10% above recent 7-day average).
- Forecast mean is often 3–5% higher than true outcome; apply a downward bias correction of 3–5% for 30-day horizons.
- Model underreacts to sustained downward trends; increase sensitivity to recent low prices by weighting last 5–7 days more heavily.
- Forecast lags behind true outcome by 1–3 days in most cases; adjust for lag by shifting forecast 1–2 days forward (or use 1-day moving average of true values as anchor).
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after sharp moves; apply a smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce volatility amplification.
